grid._clip_note: 0529-0545/0628-0637/0729-0737 added 2026-09-16 after readers on tiles 0828_0628/0829_0532/0745_0545 found the Axis Mobilization Points / Reinforcements / STAVKA Reserve tracks printed WITHIN the declared grid rectangle at rows 5-7 for columns 28-37ish (confirmed by crop: the real south edge is row 8 there, but row 6 at Bucharest's longitude, col 38+ -- an irregular boundary, same as the north edge). This is the exact case calibrate.py fit's 'unprinted' report exists to catch and this worker under-used it for (see questions log): only the geometrically out-of-image hexes were clipped after stage 1, not furniture-within-image-bounds. 3 already-read tiles (0828_0628, 0829_0532, 0745_0545) recorded these ids as placeholder 'clear' terrain with an unclear note rather than being excluded; they need a stage-6 resolution removing those hexes' terrain entries once assemble.py's missing-hex check is re-run against the corrected grid (their hexside/place data for REAL neighbouring hexes is unaffected and stays valid). SECOND ROUND (2026-09-16, after full stage 5 reading): 2329-2334/2428-2434/2529-2533/2628-2633/2729-2733/2828-2833 added after several readers independently found a 'German Reorganization Chart' plus Air Landing/Air Superiority Tables plus page credits printed within the rectangle at rows 23-28, columns 28-34ish, near the NW corner (the same corner that already has no possible NW-region control point -- see questions log). Compiled from every reader's furniture-flagged unclear/notes entries (work/smw/stage0/find_furniture.py), not re-derived from crops by this worker. Migrated via work/smw/stage0/migrate_tiles.py exactly as the first round was. THIRD ROUND (2026-09-16, during stage 6 resolution): a resolver crop-confirmed hex 2837 (and 2836/2838) sit entirely in the grey margin band above the real map's row-27 north edge, no printed content at all; a follow-up wide crop across the full row (source y=429.77, the row-28 centre line) confirmed this is true for the WHOLE of row 28, every column -- row 28 was included in the original grid rectangle purely as a stage-1 'safety margin' guess (see stage log) and should never have held real hexes anywhere. Replaced every remaining row-28 clip token with a single 'row28-full' range covering columns 1-45. This is the strongest evidence yet that the calibrate.py fit's 'unprinted' report should be read in full at stage 1 rather than trusting a rounded-up row/col margin.

vocabulary._note: read from the map's own Terrain Effects Chart / legend, upper right of the sheet, source px x 1550-1900 y 0-620; colours measured on real hexes (candidates.colour_masks), not the small legend swatches.

terrain.clear: pale cream/white paper, faint relief hatching only, ~(218,226,213)
terrain.rough: olive-tan wash over the relief hatching, ~(177,166,61); the hilly band across Germany/Slovakia/Hungary/Romania and pockets elsewhere
terrain.forest: mottled green blob, ~(150,185,130) with darker mottle, same family as PGG woods but no dark-spot contrast as strong
terrain.marsh: pale green hex with small dark-green tuft/hatch marks (not yet located on the visible map; may be absent or rare -- confirm during stage 4/5)
terrain.coastal: a hex the print draws PART water, part land (a light-blue triangle/wedge cutting the hex, the rest paper); distinct TEC terrain from all-sea, OTIH move/defense; port cities on part-water hexes (Stettin 2030, Danzig 2234, Konigsberg 2235 -- Ben's ruling 2) are 'coastal' land terrain with a port glyph, never this triangle rule alone deciding water vs land for a city hex
terrain.sea: solid light blue fill, ~(197,228,248), 'All-Sea' on the TEC: movement prohibited, blocks supply

places.city: cluster of small black rectangle blocks with black edges, bold capital name; 'City' on the TEC (OTIH move/defense, attacker cannot use Mobile CRT)
places.port: a city hex additionally marked with a circled blue anchor glyph beside/inside it; 'Port' on the TEC (OTIH move/defense, see Amphibious Movement)

hexside_lines.river: thick light-blue line (~(120,190,225)) along hexsides, rounded bends; 'River/Lake Hexside' on the TEC, +1 move, x2 defense if all attackers cross it. The print draws ONE such line style for both a river and a lake shore; no separate lake FILL terrain exists on this map (no 'lake' hex terrain in the TEC), so any hex-interior blue that is not a coastal/all-sea wedge is read as a river, not a lake.
hexside_lines.border: TWO printed dash styles, deliberately merged into one sheet element per Ben's stage-0 ruling 1: long-short dashes = 'National Border' (thin, closely spaced dashes on the TEC legend); long-long dashes with an added small red block = 'Front Line (USSR border)', which IS the USSR's western border at game start. The sheet does not distinguish them or record where the front line was.

links.rail: black hatch-tick line ('Railroad' on the TEC: full cost by rail-movement rule, 0.5 MP if used as a road; roads run alongside railroads per rule 10.6)
links.road: not a separate line the map prints as its own colour where a railroad is present (rule 10.6: 'Railroads are considered to have roads running alongside them'); confirm at stage 4/5 whether any hexes show a road with NO parallel railroad (a distinct thinner grey line) -- if none are found, 'road' may be a dead vocabulary entry for this map, a stage-0 decision to record once confirmed

markers.mobilization: a red 5-point star (Soviet Mobilization Hex) or green 5-point star (Axis Mobilization Hex) centred on a hex; a REGION overlay on top of the hex's own terrain, not a terrain of its own
markers.resource: a black oil-derrick glyph centred on a hex (Axis Resource Hex on the TEC); also a region overlay
markers.bridge: a small yellow tile with a blue lightning/river-crossing glyph, printed ON a hexside where a railroad or road crosses a river; 'Bridge' on the TEC, 0 cost to cross river
markers.compass_scale: furniture printed OVER two real hexes near the NE corner (2744: '43.5 Miles / 70 Km' scale bar; 2745: compass rose) -- not map furniture to clip (Ben's ruling 3 is about the charts AROUND the map, not icons printed on real hexes), but ignore the icon itself when reading those two hexes' terrain

candidates._note: coastal (part-water, part-land) and marsh have no colour_mask yet: coastal needs a bespoke wedge-shaped presence rule (not a simple share-of-hex threshold), and no marsh hex has been located on the visible map to calibrate against. Both are read by eye at stage 5, not proposed by candidates.py, until stage 4 tuning on real tiles settles this (see questions log).
